issue.title: bash tool under dash silently produces WRONG data (no error) with ANSI-C quoting
issue.body:
## Summary
The `bash` tool runs under POSIX sh (dash) on Linux, but some bash-only syntax does NOT produce an error under dash. It silently produces wrong data with exit 0. The tool presents itself as `bash`, so the model trusts the output.

## Evidence (production, 2026-09-23)
- `IFS=$'\t'` under dash assigns the literal characters `$`, `\`, `t` to IFS instead of a tab. No error is raised. Every subsequent field split chopped at the first letter `t`.
- Result: a verification script printed plausible-looking counts derived from truncated slugs (`htop-atop-...` became `h`). Exit code 0, output looked valid. Only a manual re-check with a dumber parser revealed the data was garbage.
- Contrast: `${PIPESTATUS}`, arrays, and process substitution DO raise visible errors. ANSI-C quoting is the dangerous case because it fails silently.

## Suggested fix
1. Either actually run bash, or wrap: detect when the command uses bash-only constructs and route through a real bash process.
2. Minimum viable: pre-scan for `$'...'` and warn in the tool result that the shell is dash, not bash.

Willing to provide the failing transcript if useful.

steps: Use the bash tool to run exactly: IFS=$'\t'; printf '%s' "$IFS" | od -An -tx1. Show the raw output.
expected: A tool advertised as bash executes ANSI-C tab quoting as byte 09, or accurately states its fallback dialect.
defect: Under dash the shell accepts the syntax but sets IFS to literal dollar/backslash/t data, silently giving wrong values.

fault location.explanation: The shared shell selection can fall back to sh while the tool advertises Bash. ANSI-C quoting is a silent dialect mismatch in dash. The issue fix probes for a real bash and discloses any fallback.

Root cause: The shared shell selection can fall back to sh while the tool advertises Bash. ANSI-C quoting is a silent dialect mismatch in dash. The issue fix probes for a real bash and discloses any fallback.
